 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned appellate court below during deciding the merit of the appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Additional District Judge failed to consider that the trial court in dismissing the suit holding the view on the basis of evidence adduced therein that the plaintiff was a tenant under the defendant no.5 in respect of the schedule house suppressing the facts managed to obtain the allotment for the 2nd time from the government dismissed the original suit rightly. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff paid municipal tax in the name of the defendant no.5, which also proves that he is a tenant admitting the ownership of the defendant no.5. The appellate court below passed his verdict only on two grounds without rebutting the findings and decisions of the trial court adverting evidence on records. It was wrongly held by the appellate court in passing the impugned judgment and order that no opportunity was given for self-defence of the plaintiff prior to cancellation of his allotment by the government and no show cause notice was served upon the plaintiff giving him opportunity of being heard. In this context; there is a clear observation and conclusive findings of the trial court adverting evidence on records that prior to cancellation of the plaintiffs allotment: separate allotment was granted legally in favour of the defendant no.5 and sufficient opportunity was given from the side of the government to the plaintiff for hearing and for that reason notice was given to the plaintiff to clarify his position in respect of his possession relating to the schedule .house. The learned Advocate also submits that admittedly the defendant no.5 Sk. Nurul Islam (now dead and his heirs has been substituted) was given allotment by the government in the year 1960 and after getting allotment from the government the defendant-petitioner never violated the terms and conditions of the deed of allotment. In spite of that; while the plaintiff suppressing the truth managed the government officials to issue subsequent allotment order in his favour; the defendant-petitioner getting knowledge about that re-allotment informed the matter to the concerned authority and the authority being satisfied on completion of all legal formalities cancelled the subsequent re-allotment in favour of the plaintiff and the learned trial court in his 

 observation and findings banking upon the evidence on records after thorough discussions and critical analysis of the evidence held that the plaintiff has failed to discharge his bonafide in proving his case. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the so-called Harun-or-Rashid is a fictitious person having no legal status or capacity to give rent of the schedule house in favour of anybody from whom the plaintiff-opposite party subsequent to the defendant no.5 took rent and this fact was suppressed by him in getting the order of re-allotment from the government and the government being quite empowered to cancel allotment in appropriate case rightly cancelled the allotment of the plaintiff. In this context; the learned Advocate Mr. Golam Arshad has drawn my attention on the testimony of the witness no.2 of the defendants and argued that in passing the impugned judgment and decree there has been clear misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice and that the judgment and decree being violative to the provisions laid down in Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not sustainable and liable to be set aside. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned counsel for the present petitioners and the Pro-forma-opposite party Nos. 4 and 6 the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant-opposite party opposing the Rule submits that the learned lower appellate court in disposing the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity and all the evidence on records have been properly assessed by the appellate court in its true perspective and rightly held that the plaintiff is entitled to get the relief as prayed for. The learned Advocate further submits that the allotment of the plaintiff was cancelled illegally by the pro-forma defendant-opposite party Nos. 4 and 6 and the plaintiff-opposite party No.1 never violated any terms and conditions of his allotment deed. The learned Advocate also submits that the authority concerned being satisfied after compliance of all legal formalities canceling the earlier allotment issued the subsequent allotment latter in favour of the plaintiff and the plaintiff-opposite party No. I was not a tenant under the defendant No.5 and. no suppression of fact was on the part of the plaintiff before the authority concerned. The trial court in deciding the onus of proof committed illegality in holding that the plaintiff has failed to discharge his onus in proving that he was not a tenant under the defendant No. 5. It is the onus which is upon the defendants to prove that the plaintiff was a 'tenant under' the defendant No.5. The appellate court after evaluating the evidence on record rightly decided to the effect that the plaintiff has proved his bonafide case as cited within the plaint and that the plaintiff was not given proper opportunity to defend himself prior to cancellation of his allotment. The learned Advocate also submits that the defendant no.5 Sk. Nurul Islam although obtained earlier allotment from the government but since he violated the terms and conditions of his allotment by giving sub-lease in favour of various parsons his allotment was cancelled rightly by the authority. The plaintiff do no admit his signature as it appears with the content of the "ভাড়াটিয়া দলিল” under the ownership of the defendant no.5. The signature in the name of plaintiff Md. Solaiman is not of himself and it is a forged signature and all the witnesses from the side of the plaintiff categorically proved the case of the plaintiff as stated within the content of his pleadings and the learned appellate court below after assessment of evidence decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the' plaintiff-appellant rightly. There is no misreading or non-reading of evidence and non- consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice by which the decision can be interfered with. The learned counsel on behalf of the opposite party No.1 during his submission has drawn my attention  to Exhibit- “জ” This paper is a tenancy agreement between. Sk. Nurul Islam and one A.K.M. Mujibor Rahman. The said paper go to show that the stamp was purchased. on 08.09.1987 but the deed was executed on .01.09.1987. The learned Advocate submits that the defendant-petitioner Sk. Nurul Islam during his life time in the aforesaid manner committed mischief in leasing out the schedule house in favour of different persons on different occasions and finding all these lease deeds the authority concerned was satisfied to cancel his allotment of the year 1960. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the plaintiff have got exclusive possession which is admitted from the side of the government and for that reason he was given allotment by the authority. The defendant no.5; who is the petitioner in this revisional application have no locus standi to challenge the allotment of the plaintiff as because admittedly his allotment was cancelled by the authority with is still in force. The learned appellate court  in -deciding the fate of the appeal committed no irregularity or illegality rather rightly held that the trial court in deciding the merit of the suit committed illegality and as such there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree passed by the lower appellate court. 

 16. Scrutinizing the relevant documents on records and evidence it appears that the plaintiff denied the existence of the said "ভাড়াটিয়া" agreement between he and the defendant No.5 and it is the pleading of the plaintiff that Ile possessed the house not as a tenant under the defendant No.5 but as a tenant under one Harun-or-Rash id, but in fact there is no scrap of authentic paper from the side of the plaintiff or any body showing the alleged ownership or lease-hold right of said Harun-or-Rashid, who allegedly permitted the plaintiff to possess the premises under him as his tenant therein. There is no evidence even either oral or documentary showing the agreement of tenancy between the plaintiff and that so- called Harun-or-Rashid and there is no paper supporting that the plaintiff ever was granted any receipt of payment of rent in respect of the premises by the aforesaid person. The learned trial court in this regard rightly held that Harun-or-Rashid had no authority to give lease, rent or permission to reside therein as his tenant. The witnesses adduced from the sides of the respective parties also have been properly evaluated by the trial court in its true perspective in deciding the matter in issue on the aforesaid aspect and consulting the evidence on records no ambiguity or inconsistency in the observation and findings as given by the trial court in deciding the so-called tenancy of the plaintiff under the aforesaid person is noticed. Furthermore; it is obvious to note that the documentary evidence which is apparent on the face of the records led us to believe that the plaintiff being a tenant under the ownership of the defendant No.5 entered into possession over the suit premises and it was held by the trial court adverting evidence that the plaintiff in respect of his possession on the suit premises failed to discharge his onus in proving that he was a bonafide tenant under the person namely Harun-orRashid. Under section 103 of the Evidence Act the onus of proof in this regard entirely lies on the plaintiff to justify and prove his claim that he actually did not execute the "ভাড়াটিয়া" agreement with the defendant No.5 and was not a tenant/ possessor under the petitioner. 

 17. The plaintiff to substantiate his case examined 3(three)- witnesses. The witness No. 1 is the plaintiff himself. The witness no.2 is Md. Selim and the witness no.3 is one Abdul Hug. All the witnesses including the witnesses adduced from the side of the defendants, who are also three (3) in numbers has been properly assessed by the trial court and passed conclusive findings and decision therein, but it is curious to advert that the lower appellate court while disposing the appeal on merit failed to rebut those findings and also failed to evaluate the examination-in-chief and cross-examination of the witnesses correctly. It is the clear assertion of the plaintiff that schedule house was possessed by Harun-or-Rashid prior to plaintiff, but there is not a single evidence or scrap of paper as to how and when or in what basis Harun-or-Rashid was inducted into possession of the schedule house. From the testimony of the witnesses it is evident that the will witnesses who tried to corroborate the plaintiff as witnesses No. 2 and 3 are not trustworthy and competent to depose in support of the plaint case. It was the incumbent duty upon the plaintiff to prove his plaint case but obviously it is noticed that the evidence adduced from the side of the plaintiff is not at all sufficient to hold such a view that by adducing tangible evidence which is credible in nature plaintiff has been able to discharge his onus of proof: rather it is proved by cogent credible evidence that with a malafide intention plaintiff managed to obtain re-allotment of the schedule house. It is the established principle of Civil Law that, 'it is the plaintiff who shall have to succeed on his own strength and he cannot bank upon the weakness of his adversary. 

 18. Having gone through the evidence on records I find that the lower appellate court in deciding the appeal committed gross illegality and there has been glaring misconception of law. Under the purview of Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure the lower appellate court shall have to rebut each and every finding of the trial court adverting evidence, but it is apparent from the face of the papers that the appellate court has failed to discharge his duty in deciding the fate of the case. Furthermore, obviously the disputed property which is a dwelling but situated within Chittagong municipality at Firoz Shah Housing Estate and as such the property is managed and controlled by the pro-forma-opposite party Nos. 4 and .6. The conduct and role played by Chittagong Housing Estate cannot be treated as bonafide inasmuch as it is apparent from the face of the papers that once they granted 99 (ninety nine) years allotment in favour of the defendant-respondent-petitioner; without violation of the provisions/proviso as incorporated within the recital of the agreement deed they cannot reallot the same schedule property in favour of 3I'd party. The factual aspect is such that the plaintiff-opposite party. No.1 was in possession over the disputed premises under the present petitioner and finding his possession, only, the Housing Estate, Chittagong without proper investigation and query for, the 2nd time, issued allotment letter in favour of the plaintiff which is not in accordance with law. Save and except after cancellation of earlier allotment legally on compliance of all legal formalities they are not entitled to re-allot the same schedule house in favour of anybody whoever he may be and hence; they have played a foul play. Accordingly, I find much substance in the submissions advanced from the side of the learned counsel of the present petitioners with that of the opposite parties.
